MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT MSA-976084 — SERVICE LEVEL SCHEDULE, AMENDMENTS AND MONTHLY REVIEW
Extract assembled for the coverage decision. Pagination removed. Notes in square brackets were added by the file clerk.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — SERVICE LEVELS
======================================================================
1.1. Uptime calculation. Monthly uptime percentage = (available minutes) / (total minutes in the month minus excluded minutes) x 100, rounded to three decimals.
1.2. Excluded minutes. Minutes of scheduled maintenance performed within the published maintenance window and minutes of force majeure are excluded from both the numerator and the denominator.
1.3. Customer-caused outages. Minutes of unavailability caused by the customer's own equipment, credentials or configuration are not counted as downtime but remain in the denominator.
1.4. Scheduled maintenance outside the window. Maintenance performed outside the published window counts as downtime in full.
1.5. Service credit schedule (original): monthly uptime at or above 99.9%: no credit; at or above 99.5% but below 99.9%: 5% of the monthly fee; at or above 99.0% but below 99.5%: 10%; below 99.0%: 25%.
1.6. Claims. Credits must be claimed in writing within 30 days after the end of the month and are applied to the next invoice.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — OPERATING PROCEDURES
======================================================================
2.1. Maintenance notices. Scheduled maintenance is announced at least 72 hours in advance through the status page. Maintenance that starts inside the window but runs beyond it counts as downtime for the minutes outside the window.
2.2. Monitoring. Availability is measured by the provider's monitoring system from three regions at one-minute intervals. A minute is unavailable if the service fails the health check from at least two regions.
2.3. Incident classification. Each incident is classified by the provider within 10 business days after it closes; the customer may dispute a classification within 30 days by giving written reasons. Disputed classifications are reviewed by the service manager (Fenna Iversen).
2.4. Reporting. A monthly service report is issued within 10 business days after the month end and contains the incident log, the uptime calculation and any credit due.
2.5. Data handling. The provider processes customer data only as instructed and in accordance with the data processing schedule. Backups are retained for 60 days.
2.6. Definitions. 'Available minutes' means minutes in the month in which the service passed the health check. 'Published maintenance window' means the window shown in the service description at the start of the month.
2.7. Credit application. Credits are applied to the invoice for the month after the report and are not paid in cash. Credits do not accumulate beyond the monthly fee.
2.8. Force majeure. Neither party is liable for delay or failure caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including natural disasters, war, and failures of public networks, provided the affected party notifies the other promptly.
2.9. Dispute resolution. Disputes about a service report are escalated to the account managers, then to the executives named in the agreement, before either party starts proceedings.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — GENERAL TERMS
======================================================================
3.1. Duties after loss. The customer must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 90 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
3.2. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the customer failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
3.3. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
3.4. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
3.5. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the customer has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
3.6. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 14 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
3.7. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
3.8. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the customer beyond $500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
3.9. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the customer shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT 6 (effective 20 May 2026): for contracts renewed on or after the effective date, the schedule thresholds are 99.95% (no credit), 99.7% (5%), 99.2% (10%), below 99.2% (25%). Contracts renewed earlier remain on the original schedule until their next renewal.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — MONTHLY REVIEW, CONTRACT MSA-976084
======================================================================
Contract MSA-976084 between Halcyon Systems (provider) and Hollowell Foods (customer). Renewed effective 9 February 2026. Month under review: May (30 days, 43,200 minutes). Published maintenance window: Sundays 01:00-05:00.
Incident log (durations already reconciled with the monitoring system):
- INC-66448: 20 minutes, classified 'force majeure'
- INC-76724: 90 minutes, classified 'force majeure'
- INC-68307: 150 minutes, classified 'scheduled in window'
- INC-14708: 48 minutes, classified 'customer caused'
- INC-70934: 65 minutes, classified 'unplanned'
[Account manager note, Yusuf Delacroix: uptime 99.849% against the MSA schedule (99.9% / 99.5% / 99.0%) gives a 5% credit.]

question.instructions: Which service credit tier applies to contract MSA-976084 for the month under review?

rationale: (1) Excluded from the calculation (scheduled within the window, customer-caused, force majeure): 308 min; counted downtime: 65 min. (2) Uptime = (42940 - 65) / 42940 = 99.849% (scheduled-window and force-majeure minutes are removed from the denominator; customer-caused minutes stay in it). (3) Contract renewed before 20 May 2026: original credit tiers apply. (4) 99.849% falls in the 5% credit tier.

1. 'Pre-existing condition' means any injury, sickness or condition for which the insured received treatment, advice, a diagnosis, or a change in prescribed medication within the 180 days before the policy purchase date.

======================================================================
2.1. Loss settlement. Losses are settled at the cost to repair or replace with materials of like kind and quality, without deduction for depreciation, provided repair or replacement is completed within 180 days of the loss; otherwise on an actual cash value basis until completion.

2.3. Debris removal. We will pay the reasonable expense of removing debris of covered property after a covered loss, up to 5% of the limit that applies to the damaged property, as an additional amount of insurance.
2.4. Glass replacement. Loss for damage to glass caused by a covered peril includes the cost of replacing with safety glazing material when required by ordinance or law.
2.5. Emergency mitigation. Where water has escaped, the insured must arrange drying and dehumidification within 72 hours of discovery; the cost is covered as part of the loss up to $10,000.

======================================================================
PART D — CONDITIONS
======================================================================
3.1. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
3.2. Recovered property. If the insured or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the insured must notify us. The property may be returned to the insured, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
3.3. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
3.4. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
3.5. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
3.6. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the insured shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
3.7. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the insured beyond $250 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
3.8. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 15% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 60 consecutive days.

======================================================================
6.1. Cancellation because of a change of mind, financial circumstances, or business obligations, except as provided by a Cancel-for-Any-Reason rider.

7.1. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 2% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the insured.

question.instructions: Is any part of the building water damage in claim CLM-9695397 payable under the policy?

criteria.true: Some amount is payable (with or without a sublimit).

Extract assembled for the coverage decision. Pagination removed. Notes in square brackets were added by the file clerk.

======================================================================
PART A — POLICY DECLARATIONS
======================================================================
Policyholder: Hiro Ellery
Policy number: TR-72111034
Plan: Compass Standard
Policy purchase date: 9 October 2025
Trip cost insured: $6,100

======================================================================
PART B — DEFINITIONS
======================================================================
1. 'Pre-existing condition' means any injury, sickness or condition for which the insured received treatment, advice, a diagnosis, or a change in prescribed medication within the 90 days before the policy purchase date.
2. 'Stable' means that, in the 60 days before the policy purchase date, the condition had no new symptoms, no change in treatment or medication, and no hospitalisation.
3. 'Known event' means a government travel advisory, strike, natural disaster or outbreak that was announced or publicly reported before the policy purchase date.
4. 'Non-refundable trip cost' means prepaid amounts that the travel supplier will not refund, as shown in the booking statement.
5. 'Policy purchase date' means the date shown in the declarations on which the premium was paid.

======================================================================
PART C — COVERAGES
======================================================================
2.1. Pair or set. In case of loss to a pair or set we may elect to repair or replace any part to restore the pair or set to its value before the loss, or to pay the difference between actual cash value before and after the loss.
2.2. Loss settlement. Losses are settled at the cost to repair or replace with materials of like kind and quality, without deduction for depreciation, provided repair or replacement is completed within 180 days of the loss; otherwise on an actual cash value basis until completion.
2.3. Reasonable repairs. We will pay the reasonable cost incurred by the insured for necessary measures taken solely to protect covered property from further damage after a covered loss, up to $1,000 without prior approval. This does not increase the limit of liability.
2.4. Fungi and rot. We pay up to $10,000 for the removal of fungi, wet or dry rot resulting from a covered loss, including the cost of testing the air and property.
2.5. Insuring agreement. We will pay for direct physical loss to covered property caused by a peril insured against, unless the loss is excluded or limited in this contract. The most we will pay for any one occurrence is the applicable limit shown in the declarations, less the deductible.

======================================================================
PART D — CONDITIONS
======================================================================
3.1. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
3.2. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the insured failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
3.3. Recovered property. If the insured or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the insured must notify us. The property may be returned to the insured, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
3.4. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 10% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 60 consecutive days.
3.5. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
3.6. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 1 year after the date of loss.
3.7. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $2,500 per occurrence.
3.8. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the insured committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
3.9. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 3% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the insured.
3.10. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the insured beyond $250 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
3.11. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the insured shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
3.12. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the insured and pay within 30 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.

======================================================================
PART E — TRIP CANCELLATION EXCLUSIONS (SECTION 6)
======================================================================
6.1. Cancellation because of a change of mind, financial circumstances, or business obligations, except as provided by a Cancel-for-Any-Reason rider.
6.2. Cancellation caused by a pre-existing condition. Exception 6.2.1: this exclusion does not apply if the condition was stable, in which case we pay the non-refundable trip cost subject to the pre-existing-condition sublimit shown in the schedule.
6.3. Cancellation caused by a known event.
6.4. Cancellation because a travel supplier ceases operations, unless the Supplier Default endorsement is on file.
6.5. Cancellation caused by war, nuclear hazard, or the insured's intentional act.
6.6. Expenses that are refundable, recoverable from any other source, or paid with frequent-traveller points.

======================================================================
PART F — GENERAL EXCLUSIONS AND CONDITIONS
======================================================================
7.1. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 10% of the Coverage A limit.
7.2. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
7.3. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
7.4. Cancellation. The insured may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 21 days before the effective date, or 30 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
7.5. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 21 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
7.6. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
7.7. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the insured as interests appear. Denial of the insured's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
7.8. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.
7.9. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.

======================================================================
PART G — ENDORSEMENTS
======================================================================
ENDORSEMENT CFAR-64 — CANCEL FOR ANY REASON. If bought no later than 21 days after the first trip payment, this rider pays 75% of the non-refundable trip cost when the insured cancels for a reason not otherwise covered, provided the cancellation is made at least 48 hours before departure. A rider purchased outside that window is void and the premium is refunded. [clerk: rider offered, not purchased]

======================================================================
PART H — CLAIM FILE CLM-3950247
======================================================================

Non-refundable trip cost per booking statement: $6,100. Pre-existing-condition sublimit per schedule: $2,500.
Claim narrative (Maren Tremblay): The insured cancelled on 16 January 2026 on the advice of their physician because of a back condition. The physician's statement records the last change in treatment on 11 June 2025 and no change in medication or symptoms in the 5 days before the policy purchase date.

criteria.deny_maintenance_lapse: Deny: service overdue by more than 45 days with no booked visit (Exclusion 4.4).

rationale: (1) Overdue by 10 days (not more than 45), so the maintenance exclusion does not apply. (2) 9 months of documented deterioration is at least 9, so the failure is wear and tear. Extract assembled for the coverage decision. Pagination removed. Notes in square brackets were added by the file clerk.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Oakhaven Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Ridgeway Industries reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.2. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.3. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.4. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Sanne Ferreira's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-46 and attached to the employee's file.
3.5. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.6. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.7. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.8. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
4.2. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.3. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 30 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.4. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $2,500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.5. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.6. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.7. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the employee as interests appear. Denial of the employee's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
4.8. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
4.9. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 30 days before the effective date, or 90 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
4.10. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $2,500 per occurrence.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-56 (effective 12 June 2025): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,500; G2 $9,000; G3 $13,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 5 km; to new workplace 37 km.
Household: spouse and one child relocated with the employee.

3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.

5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
3.1. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.

3.5. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.6. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.7. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.8. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.

======================================================================
This policy sets out when Orchard Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.2. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.3. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Cerys Villanueva's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-62 and attached to the employee's file.
3.4. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.5. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.6. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.7. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the employee and pay within 30 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.
4.2. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.3. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.

SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Vantage Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Tomasz Tremblay's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-61 and attached to the employee's file.
3.2. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.3. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.4. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.5. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 45 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.6. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.7. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.8. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the employee as interests appear. Denial of the employee's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.

4.4. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
4.5. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.6. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $250 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.7. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 2 years after the date of loss.
4.8. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 30 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.9. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $5,000 per occurrence.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-93 (effective 14 September 2025): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,500; G2 $10,000; G3 $12,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-3589055 for the building water damage be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
criteria.deny_repeated_leakage: Deny: the repeated-seepage exclusion (4.3) bars the loss and the concealed-water exception does not restore it.
criteria.pay_within_10000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $10,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_15000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $15,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_estimate_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the repair estimate minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was without furnishings and empty for 105 days (more than 90), so it was vacant under the definitions. (3) 25 days is at least 10 days, so the water is 'repeated seepage or leakage'. (4) The concealed-water exception does not apply: the leak was not concealed. (5) Decision: deny as repeated seepage with no exception.

Extract assembled for the coverage decision. Pagination removed. Notes in square brackets were added by the file clerk.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — SERVICE LEVELS
======================================================================
1.1. Uptime calculation. Monthly uptime percentage = (available minutes) / (total minutes in the month minus excluded minutes) x 100, rounded to three decimals.
1.2. Excluded minutes. Minutes of scheduled maintenance performed within the published maintenance window and minutes of force majeure are excluded from both the numerator and the denominator.
1.3. Customer-caused outages. Minutes of unavailability caused by the customer's own equipment, credentials or configuration are not counted as downtime but remain in the denominator.
1.4. Scheduled maintenance outside the window. Maintenance performed outside the published window counts as downtime in full.
1.5. Service credit schedule (original): monthly uptime at or above 99.9%: no credit; at or above 99.5% but below 99.9%: 5% of the monthly fee; at or above 99.0% but below 99.5%: 10%; below 99.0%: 25%.
1.6. Claims. Credits must be claimed in writing within 30 days after the end of the month and are applied to the next invoice.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — OPERATING PROCEDURES
======================================================================
2.1. Reporting. A monthly service report is issued within 5 business days after the month end and contains the incident log, the uptime calculation and any credit due.
2.2. Data handling. The provider processes customer data only as instructed and in accordance with the data processing schedule. Backups are retained for 60 days.
2.3. Termination for chronic failure. If the uptime falls into the 25% credit tier in any three months of a rolling six-month period, the customer may terminate the affected service on 45 days' notice without penalty.
2.4. Incident classification. Each incident is classified by the provider within 15 business days after it closes; the customer may dispute a classification within 45 days by giving written reasons. Disputed classifications are reviewed by the service manager (Yusuf Villanueva).
2.5. Credit application. Credits are applied to the invoice for the month after the report and are not paid in cash. Credits do not accumulate beyond the monthly fee.
2.6. Maintenance notices. Scheduled maintenance is announced at least 72 hours in advance through the status page. Maintenance that starts inside the window but runs beyond it counts as downtime for the minutes outside the window.
2.7. Monitoring. Availability is measured by the provider's monitoring system from three regions at one-minute intervals. A minute is unavailable if the service fails the health check from at least two regions.
2.8. Definitions. 'Available minutes' means minutes in the month in which the service passed the health check. 'Published maintenance window' means the window shown in the service description at the start of the month.
2.9. Dispute resolution. Disputes about a service report are escalated to the account managers, then to the executives named in the agreement, before either party starts proceedings.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — GENERAL TERMS
======================================================================
3.1. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the customer failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
3.2. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the customer shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
3.3. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the customer beyond $250 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
3.4. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 10% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 30 consecutive days.
3.5. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
3.6. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $2,500 per occurrence.
3.7. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the customer and pay within 60 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.
3.8. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 3 years after the date of loss.
3.9. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 14 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
3.10. Recovered property. If the customer or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the customer must notify us. The property may be returned to the customer, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT 3 (effective 13 December 2025): for contracts renewed on or after the effective date, the schedule thresholds are 99.95% (no credit), 99.7% (5%), 99.2% (10%), below 99.2% (25%). Contracts renewed earlier remain on the original schedule until their next renewal.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — MONTHLY REVIEW, CONTRACT MSA-648392
======================================================================

Incident log (durations already reconciled with the monitoring system):

1. 'Vacant' means that the dwelling contains no furnishings or contents sufficient for normal residential use and no one has lived in it for more than 45 consecutive days.

4.1. Earth movement, including earthquake, landslide, mudflow, sinkhole, subsidence, or earth sinking, rising or shifting, whether caused by or resulting from human or animal forces or any act of nature.
4.2. Water from flood, surface water, waves, tidal water, or overflow of a body of water, or spray from any of these, whether or not driven by wind; water that backs up through sewers or drains except as provided by endorsement.

4.7. Vacancy: loss to the building caused by water, freezing, vandalism, glass breakage or theft while the dwelling is vacant. PART H — CLAIM FILE CLM-7669384
======================================================================
Claim CLM-7669384. Insured: Fenna Jaramillo. Residence premises: 252 Elm Court, Mumbai. Date of loss (discovery): 4 January 2026.
Current term: renewed effective 26 September 2025, expiring 26 September 2026. Deductible $1,500. Coverage A limit $410,000.
Adjuster's narrative (Leif Zanetti): The insured returned from a stay with family after 46 consecutive days away. From Farid Grieg to Emeka Kowalczyk, 21 January 2026: Confirmed. Note that the customer's broker has asked to be copied on the outcome letter. Please also check whether any endorsement or amendment on the file changes the figures before we draft the letter; the base text alone is not the whole story.

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-7669384 for the building water damage be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
criteria.deny_repeated_leakage: Deny: the repeated-seepage exclusion (4.3) bars the loss and the concealed-water exception does not restore it.
criteria.pay_within_10000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $10,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_12500_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $12,500 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_estimate_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the repair estimate minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 46 days (more than 45), so it was unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. (3) 23 days is at least 21 days, so the water is 'repeated seepage or leakage'. (4) The concealed-water exception applies: the water was hidden and unknown to the insured, so cover is restored subject to the sublimit. (5) The term was renewed on or after 29 May 2025, so the concealed-water sublimit is $12,500. (6) Decision: pay, subject to the $12,500 sublimit ($5,000 - $1,500 = $3,500, capped at $12,500 = $3,500).

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Thistle Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 60 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Yusuf Ueda's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-60 and attached to the employee's file.
3.2. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 5 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.3. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.4. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.5. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.6. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.7. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.8. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 60 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.2. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 2 years after the date of loss.
4.3. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
4.4. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 3% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.5. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 14 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.6. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 14 days before the effective date, or 60 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
4.7. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.8. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 5% of the Coverage A limit.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-43 (effective 28 June 2025): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $6,500; G2 $10,000; G3 $12,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================
SECTION 6 — CASE FILE REL-296468
======================================================================
Case REL-296468. Employee: Zofia Ferreira (EMP-36180), grade G1. Former workplace: Athens office. New workplace: Sao Paulo plant. Start date at new workplace: 1 July 2025.
Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 8 km; to new workplace 60 km.
Household: spouse and one child relocated with the employee. Approved unpaid leave: 14 days during the claim period.
Claim submitted 28 November 2025 with receipts totalling $3,300 (removal contractor, travel, temporary accommodation 12 nights).
[HR assistant note, Bram Oduya: claim came 150 days after the start date, past the 120-day limit — decline.]

question.instructions: How should relocation case REL-296468 be decided under the policy and its amendments?

criteria.deny_distance_test: Not eligible: the distance test is not met.
criteria.deny_late_claim: Not payable: the claim was submitted after the time limit.
criteria.reimburse_in_full: Eligible and within the applicable cap: reimburse the full receipts.

rationale: (1) The commute increases by 52 km, less than 60 km: distance test failed. (2) Deadline: 120 days after 1 July 2025 plus 14 leave days = 12 November 2025; the claim on 28 November 2025 is late. (3) Decision: not eligible, distance test failed.

3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.

5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.

3.7. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.8. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.9. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.

5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.

3.4. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 7 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.5. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Yusuf Pires's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-47 and attached to the employee's file.
3.6. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.7. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.

======================================================================
PART C — COVERAGES

2.1. Insuring agreement. We will pay for direct physical loss to covered property caused by a peril insured against, unless the loss is excluded or limited in this contract. The most we will pay for any one occurrence is the applicable limit shown in the declarations, less the deductible.
2.2. Fungi and rot. We pay up to $10,000 for the removal of fungi, wet or dry rot resulting from a covered loss, including the cost of testing the air and property.
2.3. Reasonable repairs. We will pay the reasonable cost incurred by the insured for necessary measures taken solely to protect covered property from further damage after a covered loss, up to $2,000 without prior approval. This does not increase the limit of liability.
2.4. Debris removal. We will pay the reasonable expense of removing debris of covered property after a covered loss, up to 10% of the limit that applies to the damaged property, as an additional amount of insurance.
2.5. Glass replacement. Loss for damage to glass caused by a covered peril includes the cost of replacing with safety glazing material when required by ordinance or law.

======================================================================
PART D — CONDITIONS
======================================================================
3.1. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
3.2. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the insured committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
3.3. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
3.4. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the insured as interests appear. 3.7. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the insured has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-3767268 for the building water damage be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
criteria.deny_repeated_leakage: Deny: the repeated-seepage exclusion (4.3) bars the loss and the concealed-water exception does not restore it.
criteria.pay_within_5000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $5,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_10000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $10,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_estimate_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the repair estimate minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 89 days (not more than 90), so it was neither vacant nor unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. (3) 11 days is less than 14 days, so the water is not 'repeated seepage or leakage'. (4) Decision: sudden discharge, covered in full less the deductible: $12,500.

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-5553684 for the building water damage be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
criteria.deny_repeated_leakage: Deny: the repeated-seepage exclusion (4.3) bars the loss and the concealed-water exception does not restore it.
criteria.pay_within_5000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $5,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_15000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $15,000 after the deductible.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 91 days (more than 90), so it was unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. EQUIPMENT BREAKDOWN POLICY — EXCERPTS, ENDORSEMENTS AND CLAIM FILE CLM-4676837
Extract assembled for the coverage decision. Pagination removed. Notes in square brackets were added by the file clerk.

======================================================================
PART A — POLICY DECLARATIONS
======================================================================
Policyholder: Evergreen Textiles
Policy number: EB-35543018
Form: EB-4
Inception: 28 May 2025
Deductible: $5,000 per breakdown

======================================================================
PART B — DEFINITIONS
======================================================================
1. 'Wear and tear' means gradual deterioration evidenced in service or condition reports over a period of 9 months or more before the breakdown.
2. 'Sudden electrical event' means an electrical surge, arcing or lightning strike recorded by the site power-quality monitor or the utility on the day of the breakdown.
3. 'Service interval' means the manufacturer's scheduled maintenance interval shown in the equipment schedule. A service is 'overdue' by the number of days elapsed after the interval date.
4. 'Breakdown' means sudden and accidental physical damage to covered equipment that requires repair or replacement.
5. 'Covered equipment' means the items listed in the equipment schedule attached to the declarations.

======================================================================
PART C — COVERAGES
======================================================================
2.1. Glass replacement. Loss for damage to glass caused by a covered peril includes the cost of replacing with safety glazing material when required by ordinance or law.
2.2. Reasonable repairs. We will pay the reasonable cost incurred by the insured for necessary measures taken solely to protect covered property from further damage after a covered loss, up to $5,000 without prior approval. This does not increase the limit of liability.
2.3. Loss settlement. Losses are settled at the cost to repair or replace with materials of like kind and quality, without deduction for depreciation, provided repair or replacement is completed within 365 days of the loss; otherwise on an actual cash value basis until completion.
2.4. Fungi and rot. We pay up to $2,500 for the removal of fungi, wet or dry rot resulting from a covered loss, including the cost of testing the air and property.
2.5. Pair or set. In case of loss to a pair or set we may elect to repair or replace any part to restore the pair or set to its value before the loss, or to pay the difference between actual cash value before and after the loss.
2.6. Debris removal. We will pay the reasonable expense of removing debris of covered property after a covered loss, up to 10% of the limit that applies to the damaged property, as an additional amount of insurance.

======================================================================
PART D — CONDITIONS
======================================================================
3.1. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
3.2. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
3.3. Recovered property. If the insured or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the insured must notify us. The property may be returned to the insured, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
3.4. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the insured has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
3.5. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the insured as interests appear. Denial of the insured's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
3.6. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the insured committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
3.7. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
3.8. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $1,000 per occurrence.
3.9. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the insured and pay within 30 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.
3.10. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.

======================================================================
PART E — EXCLUSIONS (SECTION 4)
======================================================================
4.1. Loss caused by fire, explosion of a boiler, flood, earth movement, windstorm or hail (these perils are insured elsewhere).
4.2. Loss to vacuum tubes, gas tubes, brushes, belts, filters, refrigerant, lubricant or other consumable parts, except as part of a covered repair.
4.3. Loss caused by wear and tear. Exception 4.3.1: where a sudden electrical event on the day of the breakdown is documented, we will pay for the breakdown subject to the restored-cover sublimit shown in the schedule, less the deductible, even if wear and tear contributed.
4.4. Loss to equipment whose service is overdue by more than 45 days at the time of the breakdown. Exception 4.4.1: this exclusion does not apply if a service visit had been booked with a qualified contractor before the breakdown occurred.
4.5. Loss caused by testing, including hydrostatic, pneumatic or gas pressure tests, unless we have agreed in writing.
4.6. Loss caused by any defect, error or omission in design, plans, specifications or materials, except ensuing breakdown.
4.7. Loss to computer software or data, except as provided under the electronic data condition.

======================================================================
PART F — ADDITIONAL CONDITIONS
======================================================================
5.1. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 5% of the Coverage A limit.
5.2. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the insured beyond $1,000 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
5.3. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
5.4. Cancellation. The insured may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 14 days before the effective date, or 30 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
5.5. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 5% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 60 consecutive days.
5.6. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the insured failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
5.7. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 4% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the insured.

======================================================================
PART G — ENDORSEMENTS ON FILE
======================================================================
ENDORSEMENT EE-4377 — RESTORED-COVER SUBLIMIT. For policies incepting on or after 7 June 2025, the restored-cover sublimit under Exception 4.3.1 is $50,000 rather than $25,000. [clerk: filed with the schedule]

======================================================================
PART H — CLAIM FILE CLM-4676837
======================================================================
Claim CLM-4676837. Insured: Evergreen Textiles. Equipment: ammonia compressor, schedule item 13. Date of breakdown: 14 November 2025.
Policy EB-35543018: incepted 28 May 2025, 12-month term. Deductible $5,000. Restored-cover sublimit per schedule: $25,000.

RELOCATION REIMBURSEMENT POLICY (HR-33) — TEXT, AMENDMENTS AND CASE FILE REL-138224
Extract assembled for the coverage decision. Pagination removed. Notes in square brackets were added by the file clerk.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Ardent Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.2. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 45 days.
3.3. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.4. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 5 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.5. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 45 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.6. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Jiro Villanueva's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-99 and attached to the employee's file.
3.7. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.8. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.9. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.2. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
4.3. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 5% of the Coverage A limit.
4.4. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the employee shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
4.5. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.6. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.
4.7. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 2% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.8. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.9. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 5% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 60 consecutive days.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-94 (effective 15 May 2026): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,500; G2 $10,000; G3 $12,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================
SECTION 6 — CASE FILE REL-138224
======================================================================
Case REL-138224. Employee: Ximena Ferreira (EMP-20606), grade G1. Former workplace: Halifax office. New workplace: Oslo plant. Start date at new workplace: 15 April 2026.
Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 27 km; to new workplace 39 km.
Household: spouse and one child relocated with the employee. Approved unpaid leave: 25 days during the claim period.
Claim submitted 3 August 2026 with receipts totalling $2,300 (removal contractor, travel, temporary accommodation 12 nights).
[HR assistant note, Farid Sato: claim came 110 days after the start date, past the 120-day limit — decline.]

question.instructions: How should relocation case REL-138224 be decided under the policy and its amendments?

criteria.deny_distance_test: Not eligible: the distance test is not met.
criteria.deny_late_claim: Not payable: the claim was submitted after the time limit.
criteria.reimburse_in_full: Eligible and within the applicable cap: reimburse the full receipts.

rationale: (1) The commute increases by 12 km, less than 50 km: distance test failed. (2) Deadline: 120 days after 15 April 2026 plus 25 leave days = 7 September 2026; the claim on 3 August 2026 is on time. (3) Decision: not eligible, distance test failed.
