question.instructions: Is any part of the building water damage in claim CLM-9528407 payable under the policy?

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Foxglove Energy reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.2. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.3. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.4. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.5. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.6. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.7. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Vera Moreau's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-91 and attached to the employee's file.
3.8. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $2,500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.2. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.3. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 90 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.4. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.5. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 15% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 45 consecutive days.
4.6. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.7. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.8. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
4.9. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 15% of the Coverage A limit.

======================================================================

======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-78 (effective 8 February 2026): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,500; G2 $9,000; G3 $11,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

3.5. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
criteria.deny_repeated_leakage: Deny: the repeated-seepage exclusion (4.3) bars the loss and the concealed-water exception does not restore it.
criteria.pay_within_7500_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $7,500 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_12500_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $12,500 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_estimate_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the repair estimate minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 45 days (more than 30), so it was unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. (3) 16 days is at least 14 days, so the water is 'repeated seepage or leakage'. (4) The concealed-water exception does not apply: the leak was not concealed. (5) Decision: deny as repeated seepage with no exception.

This policy sets out when Granite Energy reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================

3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.2. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.3. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.4. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Gustav Coetzee's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-89 and attached to the employee's file.

3.6. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.7. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.8. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.9. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.10. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.2. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $1,000 per occurrence.
4.3. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 30 days before the effective date, or 60 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
4.4. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the employee as interests appear. Denial of the employee's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
4.5. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 4% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.6. Duties after loss. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 60 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.7. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
4.8. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $1,000 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.9. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.10. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.11. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 15% of the Coverage A limit.
4.12. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the employee shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Evergreen Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 45 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.2. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.3. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.4. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Pavel Kessler's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-14 and attached to the employee's file.
3.5. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.6. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.7. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.8. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 45 days.
3.9. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.10. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 30 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.2. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.3. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
4.4. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 5% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 60 consecutive days.
4.5. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the employee as interests appear. Denial of the employee's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
4.6. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.7. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $2,500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.8. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 1 year after the date of loss.
4.9. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 30 days before the effective date, or 30 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
4.10. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
4.11. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-53 (effective 20 October 2025): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $4,000; G2 $7,000; G3 $11,000. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================

Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 20 km; to new workplace 70 km.
Household: the employee relocated alone.

criteria.deny_late_claim: Not payable: the claim was submitted after the time limit.
criteria.reimburse_in_full: Eligible and within the applicable cap: reimburse the full receipts.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Silverbrook Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.2. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.3. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.4. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.5. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 7 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.6. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.7. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Tomasz Moreau's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-15 and attached to the employee's file.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 10% of the Coverage A limit.
4.2. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.3. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.4. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.5. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the employee as interests appear. 4.6. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.7. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 1 year after the date of loss.
4.8. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $2,500 per occurrence.
4.9. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
4.10. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 4% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.

======================================================================
PART A — POLICY DECLARATIONS
======================================================================
Policyholder: Tidewater Manufacturing
Policy number: EB-95646461
Form: EB-3
Inception: 28 April 2025
Deductible: $1,000 per breakdown

======================================================================
PART B — DEFINITIONS
======================================================================
1. 'Wear and tear' means gradual deterioration evidenced in service or condition reports over a period of 9 months or more before the breakdown.
2. 'Sudden electrical event' means an electrical surge, arcing or lightning strike recorded by the site power-quality monitor or the utility on the day of the breakdown.
3. 'Service interval' means the manufacturer's scheduled maintenance interval shown in the equipment schedule. A service is 'overdue' by the number of days elapsed after the interval date.
4. 'Breakdown' means sudden and accidental physical damage to covered equipment that requires repair or replacement.
5. 'Covered equipment' means the items listed in the equipment schedule attached to the declarations.

======================================================================
PART C — COVERAGES
======================================================================
2.1. Fungi and rot. We pay up to $5,000 for the removal of fungi, wet or dry rot resulting from a covered loss, including the cost of testing the air and property.
2.2. Debris removal. We will pay the reasonable expense of removing debris of covered property after a covered loss, up to 10% of the limit that applies to the damaged property, as an additional amount of insurance.
2.3. Glass replacement. Loss for damage to glass caused by a covered peril includes the cost of replacing with safety glazing material when required by ordinance or law.
2.4. Reasonable repairs. We will pay the reasonable cost incurred by the insured for necessary measures taken solely to protect covered property from further damage after a covered loss, up to $2,000 without prior approval. This does not increase the limit of liability.
2.5. Emergency mitigation. Where water has escaped, the insured must arrange drying and dehumidification within 72 hours of discovery; the cost is covered as part of the loss up to $4,000.

======================================================================
PART D — CONDITIONS
======================================================================
3.1. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 2 years after the date of loss.
3.2. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 4% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the insured.
3.3. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the insured failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
3.4. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
3.5. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
3.6. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
3.7. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the insured has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
3.8. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the insured shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
3.9. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the insured and pay within 90 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.
3.10. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 5% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 45 consecutive days.

======================================================================
PART E — EXCLUSIONS (SECTION 4)
======================================================================
4.1. Loss caused by fire, explosion of a boiler, flood, earth movement, windstorm or hail (these perils are insured elsewhere).
4.2. Loss to vacuum tubes, gas tubes, brushes, belts, filters, refrigerant, lubricant or other consumable parts, except as part of a covered repair.
4.3. Loss caused by wear and tear. Exception 4.3.1: where a sudden electrical event on the day of the breakdown is documented, we will pay for the breakdown subject to the restored-cover sublimit shown in the schedule, less the deductible, even if wear and tear contributed.
4.4. Loss to equipment whose service is overdue by more than 90 days at the time of the breakdown. Exception 4.4.1: this exclusion does not apply if a service visit had been booked with a qualified contractor before the breakdown occurred.
4.5. Loss caused by testing, including hydrostatic, pneumatic or gas pressure tests, unless we have agreed in writing.
4.6. Loss caused by any defect, error or omission in design, plans, specifications or materials, except ensuing breakdown.
4.7. Loss to computer software or data, except as provided under the electronic data condition.

======================================================================
PART F — ADDITIONAL CONDITIONS
======================================================================
5.1. Recovered property. If the insured or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the insured must notify us. The property may be returned to the insured, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
5.2. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 5% of the Coverage A limit.
5.3. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
5.4. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
5.5. Cancellation. The insured may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 30 days before the effective date, or 90 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
5.6. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.
5.7. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $2,500 per occurrence.

======================================================================
PART G — ENDORSEMENTS ON FILE
======================================================================
ENDORSEMENT EE-6653 — RESTORED-COVER SUBLIMIT. For policies incepting on or after 25 September 2025, the restored-cover sublimit under Exception 4.3.1 is $45,000 rather than $20,000. [clerk: filed with the schedule]

======================================================================
PART H — CLAIM FILE CLM-4019943
======================================================================
Claim CLM-4019943. Insured: Tidewater Manufacturing. Equipment: extrusion line drive, schedule item 2. Date of breakdown: 8 January 2026.
Policy EB-95646461: incepted 28 April 2025, 12-month term. Deductible $1,000. Restored-cover sublimit per schedule: $20,000.
Engineer's report (Zofia Kowalczyk): the extrusion line drive stopped at 08:45 on 8 January 2026. Site power-quality logs show no abnormal events that day. Service reports over the previous 18 months note progressive bearing noise and rising vibration readings. The last scheduled service was due 85 days before the breakdown; no visit had been booked.
Repair quotation: $24,000 (parts and labour). Business interruption: not claimed.
[Trainee note, Bram Eriksen: the service reports mention 18 month(s) of bearing noise — that is wear and tear, DENY.]

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-4019943 be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_maintenance_lapse: Deny: service overdue by more than 90 days with no booked visit (Exclusion 4.4).
criteria.deny_wear_and_tear: Deny: wear and tear (Exclusion 4.3) with no exception applying.
criteria.pay_within_20000_sublimit: Pay: cover restored by Exception 4.3.1, capped at $20,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_45000_sublimit: Pay: cover restored by Exception 4.3.1, capped at $45,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_full_repair_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the quotation minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) Overdue by 85 days (not more than 90), so the maintenance exclusion does not apply. (2) 18 months of documented deterioration is at least 9, so the failure is wear and tear. (3) The sudden-electrical-event exception does not apply: no documented surge. (4) Decision: deny as wear and tear.

1. 'Vacant' means that the dwelling contains no furnishings or contents sufficient for normal residential use and no one has lived in it for more than 90 consecutive days.

3. 'Repeated seepage or leakage' means water or steam escaping continuously or repeatedly for 14 days or longer.
4. 'Concealed water' means water that escapes within walls, floors, ceilings or under a slab, that is not visible from any living space, and whose escape is unknown to the insured until discovery.
5. 'Sudden and accidental discharge' means an escape of water that begins abruptly and is not repeated seepage or leakage.
6. 'Residence premises' means the one- or two-family dwelling where the insured resides, shown in the declarations, including structures attached to it.

======================================================================
PART C — COVERAGES
======================================================================
2.1. Emergency mitigation. Where water has escaped, the insured must arrange drying and dehumidification within 72 hours of discovery; the cost is covered as part of the loss up to $10,000.
2.2. Insuring agreement. We will pay for direct physical loss to covered property caused by a peril insured against, unless the loss is excluded or limited in this contract. The most we will pay for any one occurrence is the applicable limit shown in the declarations, less the deductible.
2.3. Reasonable repairs. We will pay the reasonable cost incurred by the insured for necessary measures taken solely to protect covered property from further damage after a covered loss, up to $5,000 without prior approval. This does not increase the limit of liability.

2.5. Glass replacement. Loss for damage to glass caused by a covered peril includes the cost of replacing with safety glazing material when required by ordinance or law.
2.6. Debris removal. We will pay the reasonable expense of removing debris of covered property after a covered loss, up to 10% of the limit that applies to the damaged property, as an additional amount of insurance.

PART D — GENERAL CONDITIONS
======================================================================
3.1. Duties after loss. The insured must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 90 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
3.2. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the insured failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
3.3. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.
3.4. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.

3.6. Recovered property. If the insured or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the insured must notify us. The property may be returned to the insured, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
3.7. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 5% of the Coverage A limit.
3.8. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the insured committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
3.9. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
3.10. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 2% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the insured.
3.11. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.

======================================================================
PART E — EXCLUSIONS (SECTION 4) AND SUBLIMITS
======================================================================
4.1. Earth movement, including earthquake, landslide, mudflow, sinkhole, subsidence, or earth sinking, rising or shifting, whether caused by or resulting from human or animal forces or any act of nature.
4.2. Water from flood, surface water, waves, tidal water, or overflow of a body of water, or spray from any of these, whether or not driven by wind; water that backs up through sewers or drains except as provided by endorsement.
4.3. Water or steam that seeps or leaks repeatedly out of plumbing, heating or cooling equipment, a fire sprinkler installation, or a domestic appliance. Exception 4.3.1: this exclusion does not apply to concealed water, in which case we will pay for the resulting damage to the building subject to the concealed-water sublimit shown in Part D, less the deductible. Exception 4.3.1 does not apply if the insured knew of the seepage or leakage before the damage was discovered.
4.4. Wear and tear, marring, deterioration, mechanical breakdown, rust or other corrosion, mould, wet or dry rot, or smog, except that resulting ensuing loss from a covered peril is covered.
4.5. Freezing of plumbing, heating or cooling equipment, a fire sprinkler installation, or a domestic appliance, unless the insured took reasonable care to keep the building heated, or turned off the water and drained the pipes.
4.6. Theft in or to a dwelling under construction, or of materials and supplies for use in the construction, until the dwelling is finished and occupied.
4.7. Vacancy: loss to the building caused by water, freezing, vandalism, glass breakage or theft while the dwelling is vacant. Exception 4.7.1: this exclusion does not apply while the dwelling is undergoing renovation under a building permit issued by the local authority. This exclusion does not apply to an unoccupied dwelling.
4.8. Power failure that originates off the residence premises, unless a covered peril ensues on the premises and then only for the ensuing loss.
4.9. Intentional loss, neglect, war, nuclear hazard and governmental action as set out in Part E.
Sublimits (Part E): concealed water $7,500 per occurrence; mould remediation $5,000; trees, shrubs and plants $1,000 per item.

======================================================================
5.1. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the insured beyond $2,500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
5.2. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the insured shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.

Denial of the insured's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
5.4. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
5.5. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the insured has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.

5.7. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 5% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 45 consecutive days.
5.8. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.

PART G — ENDORSEMENTS ON FILE
======================================================================

======================================================================
PART H — CLAIM FILE CLM-9186033
======================================================================
Claim CLM-9186033. Insured: Maren Zubair. Residence premises: 453 Yew Way, Mumbai. Date of loss (discovery): 11 August 2026.
Current term: renewed effective 18 January 2026, expiring 18 January 2027. Deductible $2,500. Coverage A limit $550,000.
Adjuster's narrative (Sanne Varga): The insured returned from an extended work assignment abroad after 85 consecutive days away. The house had been cleared of furniture and contents before the absence, pending a planned sale. On return the insured found water damage to the kitchen floor and cabinets. question.instructions: Is any part of the building water damage in claim CLM-9186033 payable under the policy?

criteria.true: Some amount is payable (with or without a sublimit).
criteria.false: The claim is excluded and nothing is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was without furnishings and empty for 85 days (not more than 90), so it was neither vacant nor unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. (3) 11 days is less than 14 days, so the water is not 'repeated seepage or leakage'. (4) Decision: sudden discharge, covered in full less the deductible: $9,200.

======================================================================
PART A — POLICY DECLARATIONS
======================================================================
Policyholder: Ridgeway Textiles
Policy number: EB-24433214
Form: EB-5
Inception: 15 March 2026
Deductible: $1,000 per breakdown

======================================================================
PART B — DEFINITIONS
======================================================================
1. 'Wear and tear' means gradual deterioration evidenced in service or condition reports over a period of 9 months or more before the breakdown.
2. 'Sudden electrical event' means an electrical surge, arcing or lightning strike recorded by the site power-quality monitor or the utility on the day of the breakdown.
3. 'Service interval' means the manufacturer's scheduled maintenance interval shown in the equipment schedule. A service is 'overdue' by the number of days elapsed after the interval date.
4. 'Breakdown' means sudden and accidental physical damage to covered equipment that requires repair or replacement.
5. 'Covered equipment' means the items listed in the equipment schedule attached to the declarations.

======================================================================
PART C — COVERAGES
======================================================================
2.1. Emergency mitigation. Where water has escaped, the insured must arrange drying and dehumidification within 72 hours of discovery; the cost is covered as part of the loss up to $2,000.
2.2. Pair or set. In case of loss to a pair or set we may elect to repair or replace any part to restore the pair or set to its value before the loss, or to pay the difference between actual cash value before and after the loss.
2.3. Reasonable repairs. We will pay the reasonable cost incurred by the insured for necessary measures taken solely to protect covered property from further damage after a covered loss, up to $1,000 without prior approval. This does not increase the limit of liability.
2.4. Insuring agreement. We will pay for direct physical loss to covered property caused by a peril insured against, unless the loss is excluded or limited in this contract. The most we will pay for any one occurrence is the applicable limit shown in the declarations, less the deductible.

======================================================================
PART D — CONDITIONS
======================================================================
3.1. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 4% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the insured.
3.2. Duties after loss. The insured must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 30 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
3.3. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
3.4. Recovered property. If the insured or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the insured must notify us. The property may be returned to the insured, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
3.5. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 1 year after the date of loss.
3.6. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the insured beyond $500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
3.7. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 10% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 30 consecutive days.
3.8. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the insured and pay within 30 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.
3.9. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
3.10. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the insured failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
3.11. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $5,000 per occurrence.
3.12. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.

======================================================================
PART E — EXCLUSIONS (SECTION 4)
======================================================================
4.1. Loss caused by fire, explosion of a boiler, flood, earth movement, windstorm or hail (these perils are insured elsewhere).
4.2. Loss to vacuum tubes, gas tubes, brushes, belts, filters, refrigerant, lubricant or other consumable parts, except as part of a covered repair.
4.3. Loss caused by wear and tear. Exception 4.3.1: where a sudden electrical event on the day of the breakdown is documented, we will pay for the breakdown subject to the restored-cover sublimit shown in the schedule, less the deductible, even if wear and tear contributed.
4.4. Loss to equipment whose service is overdue by more than 45 days at the time of the breakdown. Exception 4.4.1: this exclusion does not apply if a service visit had been booked with a qualified contractor before the breakdown occurred.
4.5. Loss caused by testing, including hydrostatic, pneumatic or gas pressure tests, unless we have agreed in writing.
4.6. Loss caused by any defect, error or omission in design, plans, specifications or materials, except ensuing breakdown.
4.7. Loss to computer software or data, except as provided under the electronic data condition.

======================================================================
PART F — ADDITIONAL CONDITIONS
======================================================================
5.1. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 30 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
5.2. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
5.3. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the insured has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
5.4. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
5.5. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the insured shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
5.6. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 10% of the Coverage A limit.
5.7. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the insured as interests appear. Denial of the insured's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
5.8. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
5.9. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the insured committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.

======================================================================

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-9226193 be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_maintenance_lapse: Deny: service overdue by more than 45 days with no booked visit (Exclusion 4.4).
criteria.deny_wear_and_tear: Deny: wear and tear (Exclusion 4.3) with no exception applying.
criteria.pay_within_20000_sublimit: Pay: cover restored by Exception 4.3.1, capped at $20,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_45000_sublimit: Pay: cover restored by Exception 4.3.1, capped at $45,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_full_repair_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the quotation minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) Overdue by 90 days (more than 45) but a visit was booked before the failure, so the maintenance exclusion does not apply. (2) 11 months of documented deterioration is at least 9, so the failure is wear and tear. (3) The sudden-electrical-event exception applies: a documented surge triggered the final failure, so cover is restored subject to the sublimit. (4) Inception before 25 March 2026: the restored-cover sublimit is $20,000. (5) Decision: pay subject to $20,000: min($17,000, $20,000) = $17,000.

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-9891785 for the building water damage be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
criteria.deny_repeated_leakage: Deny: the repeated-seepage exclusion (4.3) bars the loss and the concealed-water exception does not restore it.
criteria.pay_within_5000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $5,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_10000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $10,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_estimate_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the repair estimate minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 120 days (more than 90), so it was unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. (3) 47 days is at least 21 days, so the water is 'repeated seepage or leakage'. (4) The concealed-water exception does not apply: the leak was not concealed. (5) Decision: deny as repeated seepage with no exception.

RELOCATION REIMBURSEMENT POLICY (HR-31) — TEXT, AMENDMENTS AND CASE FILE REL-568350
Extract assembled for the coverage decision. Pagination removed. Notes in square brackets were added by the file clerk.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Ardent Energy reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.2. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.3. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.4. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.5. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.6. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 45 days.
3.7. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Cerys Oduya's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-89 and attached to the employee's file.
3.8. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 45 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.9. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.10. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.2. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.3. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 30 days before the effective date, or 90 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
4.4. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.5. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.6. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the employee shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
4.7. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 2 years after the date of loss.
4.8. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-92 (effective 10 June 2026): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,500; G2 $7,500; G3 $11,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================
SECTION 6 — CASE FILE REL-568350
======================================================================
Case REL-568350. Employee: Corin Quiroga (EMP-64560), grade G1. Former workplace: Denver office. New workplace: Vienna plant. Start date at new workplace: 13 June 2026.
Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 8 km; to new workplace 20 km.
Household: the employee relocated alone. Approved unpaid leave: 40 days during the claim period.
Claim submitted 13 September 2026 with receipts totalling $6,400 (removal contractor, travel, storage).
[HR assistant note, Pavel Ueda: claim came 92 days after the start date, past the 90-day limit — decline.]

criteria.deny_distance_test: Not eligible: the distance test is not met.
criteria.deny_late_claim: Not payable: the claim was submitted after the time limit.
criteria.reimburse_in_full: Eligible and within the applicable cap: reimburse the full receipts.

MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT MSA-634210 — SERVICE LEVEL SCHEDULE, AMENDMENTS AND MONTHLY REVIEW
Extract assembled for the coverage decision. Pagination removed. Notes in square brackets were added by the file clerk.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — SERVICE LEVELS
======================================================================
1.1. Uptime calculation. Monthly uptime percentage = (available minutes) / (total minutes in the month minus excluded minutes) x 100, rounded to three decimals.
1.2. Excluded minutes. Minutes of scheduled maintenance performed within the published maintenance window and minutes of force majeure are excluded from both the numerator and the denominator.
1.3. Customer-caused outages. Minutes of unavailability caused by the customer's own equipment, credentials or configuration are not counted as downtime but remain in the denominator.
1.4. Scheduled maintenance outside the window. Maintenance performed outside the published window counts as downtime in full.
1.5. Service credit schedule (original): monthly uptime at or above 99.9%: no credit; at or above 99.5% but below 99.9%: 5% of the monthly fee; at or above 99.0% but below 99.5%: 10%; below 99.0%: 25%.
1.6. Claims. Credits must be claimed in writing within 30 days after the end of the month and are applied to the next invoice.

======================================================================

criteria.pay_within_5000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $5,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_15000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $15,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_estimate_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the repair estimate minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 60 days (more than 30), so it was unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. 3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================

======================================================================
3.1. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.2. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.3. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.4. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.5. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 5 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.6. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.7. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Oyelaran Reinholt's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-25 and attached to the employee's file.

4.1. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 5% of the Coverage A limit.

3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.

5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.

======================================================================
3.1. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Lumen Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.2. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Nikhil Ferreira's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-26 and attached to the employee's file.
3.3. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.4. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.5. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.6. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.7. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.8. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.9. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.10. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.2. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the employee shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
4.3. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.4. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.5. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.6. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 10 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.7. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.8. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.9. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 90 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.10. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 10% of the Coverage A limit.
4.11. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-7039729 for the building water damage be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
criteria.deny_repeated_leakage: Deny: the repeated-seepage exclusion (4.3) bars the loss and the concealed-water exception does not restore it.
criteria.pay_within_10000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $10,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_15000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $15,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_estimate_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the repair estimate minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 7 days (not more than 30), so it was neither vacant nor unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. (3) 25 days is at least 10 days, so the water is 'repeated seepage or leakage'. (4) The concealed-water exception applies: the water was hidden and unknown to the insured, so cover is restored subject to the sublimit. (5) The term was renewed before 12 September 2025, so the concealed-water sublimit is $10,000. (6) Decision: pay, subject to the $10,000 sublimit ($18,000 - $1,000 = $17,000, capped at $10,000 = $10,000).

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-9805620 for the building water damage be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
criteria.deny_repeated_leakage: Deny: the repeated-seepage exclusion (4.3) bars the loss and the concealed-water exception does not restore it.
criteria.pay_within_5000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $5,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_10000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $10,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_estimate_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the repair estimate minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 120 days (more than 60), so it was unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. (3) 42 days is at least 14 days, so the water is 'repeated seepage or leakage'. (4) The concealed-water exception applies: the water was hidden and unknown to the insured, so cover is restored subject to the sublimit. (5) The term was renewed on or after 16 November 2025, so the concealed-water sublimit is $10,000. (6) Decision: pay, subject to the $10,000 sublimit ($19,000 - $1,500 = $17,500, capped at $10,000 = $10,000).
