RELOCATION REIMBURSEMENT POLICY (HR-11) — TEXT, AMENDMENTS AND CASE FILE REL-419621
Extract assembled for the coverage decision. Pagination removed. Notes in square brackets were added by the file clerk.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Pinecrest Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.2. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.3. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.4. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.5. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.6. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 7 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.7. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.8. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Orla Zubair's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-66 and attached to the employee's file.
3.9. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.10. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.2. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 15% of the Coverage A limit.
4.3. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.4. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
4.5. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 3% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.6. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.7. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 1 year after the date of loss.
4.8. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.9. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 60 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-35 (effective 7 May 2025): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $4,000; G2 $8,500; G3 $13,000. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================
SECTION 6 — CASE FILE REL-419621
======================================================================

Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 16 km; to new workplace 55 km.
Household: spouse and one child relocated with the employee.
Claim submitted 16 July 2025 with receipts totalling $12,800 (removal contractor, travel, storage).

criteria.deny_distance_test: Not eligible: the distance test is not met.
criteria.deny_late_claim: Not payable: the claim was submitted after the time limit.
criteria.reimburse_in_full: Eligible and within the applicable cap: reimburse the full receipts.

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.

======================================================================
3.1. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 45 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.2. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.3. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.4. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.5. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Quinn Ferreira's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-13 and attached to the employee's file.
3.6. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.7. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.8. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.9. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 45 days.
3.10. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.

======================================================================

Form: EB-5
Inception: 9 March 2026

======================================================================
PART B — DEFINITIONS
======================================================================

2. 'Sudden electrical event' means an electrical surge, arcing or lightning strike recorded by the site power-quality monitor or the utility on the day of the breakdown.
3. 'Service interval' means the manufacturer's scheduled maintenance interval shown in the equipment schedule. A service is 'overdue' by the number of days elapsed after the interval date.
4. 'Breakdown' means sudden and accidental physical damage to covered equipment that requires repair or replacement.
5. 'Covered equipment' means the items listed in the equipment schedule attached to the declarations.

======================================================================
PART C — COVERAGES
======================================================================
2.1. Debris removal. We will pay the reasonable expense of removing debris of covered property after a covered loss, up to 5% of the limit that applies to the damaged property, as an additional amount of insurance.
2.2. Insuring agreement. We will pay for direct physical loss to covered property caused by a peril insured against, unless the loss is excluded or limited in this contract. The most we will pay for any one occurrence is the applicable limit shown in the declarations, less the deductible.
2.3. Emergency mitigation. Where water has escaped, the insured must arrange drying and dehumidification within 72 hours of discovery; the cost is covered as part of the loss up to $2,000.
2.4. Glass replacement. Loss for damage to glass caused by a covered peril includes the cost of replacing with safety glazing material when required by ordinance or law.

======================================================================
PART D — CONDITIONS
======================================================================
3.1. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
3.2. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the insured shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
3.3. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the insured and pay within 30 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.
3.4. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
3.5. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the insured has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
3.6. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the insured failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
3.7. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 10% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 30 consecutive days.
3.8. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the insured committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
3.9. Recovered property. If the insured or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the insured must notify us. The property may be returned to the insured, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
3.10. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
3.11. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.
3.12. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the insured as interests appear. Denial of the insured's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.

======================================================================
PART E — EXCLUSIONS (SECTION 4)
======================================================================
4.1. Loss caused by fire, explosion of a boiler, flood, earth movement, windstorm or hail (these perils are insured elsewhere).
4.2. Loss to vacuum tubes, gas tubes, brushes, belts, filters, refrigerant, lubricant or other consumable parts, except as part of a covered repair.
4.3. Loss caused by wear and tear. Exception 4.3.1: where a sudden electrical event on the day of the breakdown is documented, we will pay for the breakdown subject to the restored-cover sublimit shown in the schedule, less the deductible, even if wear and tear contributed.
4.4. Loss to equipment whose service is overdue by more than 45 days at the time of the breakdown. Exception 4.4.1: this exclusion does not apply if a service visit had been booked with a qualified contractor before the breakdown occurred.
4.5. Loss caused by testing, including hydrostatic, pneumatic or gas pressure tests, unless we have agreed in writing.
4.6. Loss caused by any defect, error or omission in design, plans, specifications or materials, except ensuing breakdown.
4.7. Loss to computer software or data, except as provided under the electronic data condition.

======================================================================
PART F — ADDITIONAL CONDITIONS
======================================================================
5.1. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
5.2. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
5.3. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the insured beyond $1,000 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
5.4. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $5,000 per occurrence.
5.5. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
5.6. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 3% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the insured.
5.7. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 1 year after the date of loss.
5.8. Duties after loss. The insured must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 30 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
5.9. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 10% of the Coverage A limit.

PART G — ENDORSEMENTS ON FILE

ENDORSEMENT EE-6360 — RESTORED-COVER SUBLIMIT. For policies incepting on or after 19 March 2026, the restored-cover sublimit under Exception 4.3.1 is $35,000 rather than $20,000. [clerk: filed with the schedule]

2.7. Definitions. 'Available minutes' means minutes in the month in which the service passed the health check. 'Published maintenance window' means the window shown in the service description at the start of the month.

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-7240177 for the building water damage be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
criteria.deny_repeated_leakage: Deny: the repeated-seepage exclusion (4.3) bars the loss and the concealed-water exception does not restore it.
criteria.pay_within_10000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $10,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_20000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $20,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_estimate_less_deductible: Pay in full: no exclusion or sublimit applies; the repair estimate minus the deductible is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was without furnishings and empty for 12 days (not more than 90), so it was neither vacant nor unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. (3) 12 days is at least 10 days, so the water is 'repeated seepage or leakage'. (4) The concealed-water exception does not apply: the insured knew of the leak. (5) Decision: deny as repeated seepage with no exception.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Bluewater Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.2. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 45 days.
3.3. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.4. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 45 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.5. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.6. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Katja Lindqvist's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-84 and attached to the employee's file.
3.7. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.8. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.9. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.10. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.

======================================================================

======================================================================
4.1. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 2% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.

4.7. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 5% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 30 consecutive days.

SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Foxglove Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.2. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.3. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.4. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.5. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.6. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.7. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Wendel Ueda's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-56 and attached to the employee's file.
3.8. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.9. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.10. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.2. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 15% of the Coverage A limit.
4.3. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
4.4. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the employee shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
4.5. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.6. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 15% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 45 consecutive days.
4.7. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $2,500 per occurrence.
4.8. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the employee as interests appear. ======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Pinecrest Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.2. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.3. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.4. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Bram Oduya's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-93 and attached to the employee's file.
3.5. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.6. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.7. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.8. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.2. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.3. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.4. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 10% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 30 consecutive days.
4.5. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
4.6. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the employee shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
4.7. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 1 year after the date of loss.
4.8. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
4.9. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 90 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.10. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $2,500 per occurrence.

Extract assembled for the coverage decision. Pagination removed. Notes in square brackets were added by the file clerk.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — SERVICE LEVELS
======================================================================
1.1. Uptime calculation. Monthly uptime percentage = (available minutes) / (total minutes in the month minus excluded minutes) x 100, rounded to three decimals.
1.2. Excluded minutes. Minutes of scheduled maintenance performed within the published maintenance window and minutes of force majeure are excluded from both the numerator and the denominator.
1.3. Customer-caused outages. Minutes of unavailability caused by the customer's own equipment, credentials or configuration are not counted as downtime but remain in the denominator.
1.4. Scheduled maintenance outside the window. Maintenance performed outside the published window counts as downtime in full.
1.5. Service credit schedule (original): monthly uptime at or above 99.9%: no credit; at or above 99.5% but below 99.9%: 5% of the monthly fee; at or above 99.0% but below 99.5%: 10%; below 99.0%: 25%.
1.6. Claims. Credits must be claimed in writing within 30 days after the end of the month and are applied to the next invoice.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — OPERATING PROCEDURES
======================================================================
2.1. Monitoring. Availability is measured by the provider's monitoring system from three regions at one-minute intervals. A minute is unavailable if the service fails the health check from at least two regions.
2.2. Data handling. The provider processes customer data only as instructed and in accordance with the data processing schedule. Backups are retained for 90 days.
2.3. Force majeure. Neither party is liable for delay or failure caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including natural disasters, war, and failures of public networks, provided the affected party notifies the other promptly.
2.4. Reporting. A monthly service report is issued within 7 business days after the month end and contains the incident log, the uptime calculation and any credit due.
2.5. Termination for chronic failure. If the uptime falls into the 25% credit tier in any three months of a rolling six-month period, the customer may terminate the affected service on 45 days' notice without penalty.
2.6. Incident classification. Each incident is classified by the provider within 15 business days after it closes; the customer may dispute a classification within 45 days by giving written reasons. Disputed classifications are reviewed by the service manager (Rosa Castellan).
2.7. Dispute resolution. Disputes about a service report are escalated to the account managers, then to the executives named in the agreement, before either party starts proceedings.
2.8. Maintenance notices. Scheduled maintenance is announced at least 72 hours in advance through the status page. Maintenance that starts inside the window but runs beyond it counts as downtime for the minutes outside the window.
2.9. Definitions. 'Available minutes' means minutes in the month in which the service passed the health check. 'Published maintenance window' means the window shown in the service description at the start of the month.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — GENERAL TERMS
======================================================================
3.1. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 3 years after the date of loss.
3.2. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
3.3. Cancellation. The customer may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 21 days before the effective date, or 60 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
3.4. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 2% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the customer.
3.5. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the customer beyond $2,500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
3.6. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
3.7. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the customer and pay within 60 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.
3.8. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
3.9. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
3.10. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $2,500 per occurrence.
3.11. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 21 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
3.12. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the customer as interests appear. Denial of the customer's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT 3 (effective 5 March 2026): for contracts renewed on or after the effective date, the schedule thresholds are 99.95% (no credit), 99.7% (5%), 99.2% (10%), below 99.2% (25%). Contracts renewed earlier remain on the original schedule until their next renewal.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — MONTHLY REVIEW, CONTRACT MSA-759452
======================================================================

Incident log (durations already reconciled with the monitoring system):

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-3238251 be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_maintenance_lapse: Deny: service overdue by more than 30 days with no booked visit (Exclusion 4.4).

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Umbra Industries reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.2. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.3. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.4. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.5. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.6. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.7. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 45 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.8. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Kalinda Lindqvist's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-33 and attached to the employee's file.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 21 days before the effective date, or 30 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
4.2. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.3. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
4.4. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 3% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.5. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.6. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 10% of the Coverage A limit.
4.7. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 30 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.8. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.9. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $2,500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.10. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.
4.11. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 3 years after the date of loss.
4.12. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-20 (effective 23 May 2026): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $6,500; G2 $8,500; G3 $14,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================
SECTION 6 — CASE FILE REL-567217
======================================================================
Case REL-567217. Employee: Hiro Haldane (EMP-81849), grade G2. Former workplace: Halifax office. New workplace: Auckland plant. Start date at new workplace: 23 April 2026.
Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 40 km; to new workplace 119 km.
Household: spouse and one child relocated with the employee. Approved unpaid leave: 25 days during the claim period.
Claim submitted 13 May 2026 with receipts totalling $9,400 (removal contractor, travel, storage).
[HR assistant note, Tomasz Castellan: receipts are in order, reimburse $9,400 in full.]

question.instructions: How should relocation case REL-567217 be decided under the policy and its amendments?

criteria.deny_distance_test: Not eligible: the distance test is not met.
criteria.deny_late_claim: Not payable: the claim was submitted after the time limit.
criteria.reimburse_in_full: Eligible and within the applicable cap: reimburse the full receipts.

rationale: (1) The commute increases by 79 km, less than 80 km: distance test failed. (2) Deadline: 90 days after 23 April 2026 plus 25 leave days = 16 August 2026; the claim on 13 May 2026 is on time. (3) Decision: not eligible, distance test failed.

This policy sets out when Larkspur Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.2. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.3. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.4. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.5. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.6. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.7. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.8. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Greta Dvorak's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-71 and attached to the employee's file.
3.9. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.10. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 2% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.2. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.3. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $2,500 per occurrence.
4.4. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 30 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.5. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the employee shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.

4.7. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Ashcombe Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.2. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 5 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.3. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.4. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 45 days.
3.5. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.6. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.7. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 10% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 30 consecutive days.
4.2. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the employee shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
4.3. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.4. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 1 year after the date of loss.
4.5. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
4.6. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.
4.7. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.8. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $2,500 per occurrence.
4.9. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.10. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 30 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.11. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. This policy sets out when Silverbrook Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 60 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================

======================================================================
3.1. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Quinn Reinholt's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-67 and attached to the employee's file.
3.2. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.3. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.4. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.5. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.6. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.7. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.8. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.9. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.

======================================================================

======================================================================
4.1. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.

question.instructions: How should claim CLM-3439484 for the building water damage be decided under the policy as it stands?

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.

SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Copperleaf Industries reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.2. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.3. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.4. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.5. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.6. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.7. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.8. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Corin Brandt's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-49 and attached to the employee's file.
3.9. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.

======================================================================

This policy sets out when Ironwood Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.2. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.3. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.4. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Dario Grieg's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-11 and attached to the employee's file.
3.5. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.6. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.7. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.8. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 7 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.
4.2. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.3. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 15% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 30 consecutive days.

Denial of the employee's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
4.5. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 60 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.6. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.7. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $1,000 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Granite Energy reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.2. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.3. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.4. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.5. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.6. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.7. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.8. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Fenna Oduya's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-99 and attached to the employee's file.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $1,000 per occurrence.
4.2. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.3. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 2% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.4. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 90 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.5. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.
4.6. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the employee shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
4.7. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.8. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.9. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 10 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.10. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-26 (effective 27 April 2026): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $6,500; G2 $8,500; G3 $14,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================
SECTION 6 — CASE FILE REL-772495
======================================================================

Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 31 km; to new workplace 101 km.
Household: spouse and one child relocated with the employee.
Claim submitted 26 October 2026 with receipts totalling $6,300 (removal contractor, travel, storage).

question.instructions: How many exclusions bar cover for the building water damage in claim CLM-1739325, after applying any exceptions?

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
