criteria.pay_within_7500_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $7,500 after the deductible.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Northgate Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 60 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.2. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.3. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.4. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.5. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.6. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.7. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.2. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
4.3. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.4. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 2% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.5. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
4.6. Definitions of general application. In this contract 'we' and 'us' mean the insurer that issued it, and 'you' means the employee shown on the declarations page. 'Business day' means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday at the place shown in the declarations.
4.7. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the employee as interests appear. Denial of the employee's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
4.8. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 14 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-66 (effective 22 December 2025): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $4,500; G2 $7,500; G3 $13,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================

======================================================================

Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 32 km; to new workplace 44 km.
Household: the employee relocated alone. Approved unpaid leave: 40 days during the claim period.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Westmark Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.2. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Oyelaran Villanueva's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-23 and attached to the employee's file.
3.3. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.4. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.5. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.6. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.7. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.8. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.9. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.10. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.2. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
4.3. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $2,500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.4. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 10 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.5. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.6. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.7. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
4.8. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.9. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.10. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 15% of the Coverage A limit.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-71 (effective 10 April 2025): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,000; G2 $7,000; G3 $13,000. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================
SECTION 6 — CASE FILE REL-904355
======================================================================
Case REL-904355. Employee: Petra Marchetti (EMP-27943), grade G2. Former workplace: Cape Town office. New workplace: Athens plant. Start date at new workplace: 11 March 2025.
Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 27 km; to new workplace 39 km.
Household: spouse and one child relocated with the employee.
Claim submitted 8 June 2025 with receipts totalling $2,200 (removal contractor, travel, storage).

This policy sets out when Redfern Industries reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 40 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Corin Haldane's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-53 and attached to the employee's file.
3.2. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.3. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.4. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.5. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.6. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.7. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 45 days.
3.8. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.2. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 1 year after the date of loss.
4.3. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 21 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.4. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.

RELOCATION REIMBURSEMENT POLICY (HR-36) — TEXT, AMENDMENTS AND CASE FILE REL-974521
Extract assembled for the coverage decision. Pagination removed. Notes in square brackets were added by the file clerk.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Ardent Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Gustav Moreau's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-75 and attached to the employee's file.
3.2. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.3. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.4. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.5. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.6. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.7. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.8. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.9. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.10. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 14 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.2. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.3. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.4. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
4.5. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.6. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 14 days before the effective date, or 30 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
4.7. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $5,000 per occurrence.
4.8. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-66 (effective 9 October 2026): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,000; G2 $7,000; G3 $13,000. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================
SECTION 6 — CASE FILE REL-974521
======================================================================
Case REL-974521. Employee: Fenna Whitlock (EMP-10442), grade G1. Former workplace: Perth office. New workplace: Mumbai plant. Start date at new workplace: 11 July 2026.
Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 5 km; to new workplace 85 km.
Household: spouse and one child relocated with the employee.
Claim submitted 29 October 2026 with receipts totalling $3,300 (removal contractor, travel, utility connections).
[HR assistant note, Greta Hoffmann: claim came 110 days after the start date, past the 120-day limit — decline.]

question.instructions: How should relocation case REL-974521 be decided under the policy and its amendments?

criteria.deny_distance_test: Not eligible: the distance test is not met.
criteria.deny_late_claim: Not payable: the claim was submitted after the time limit.
criteria.reimburse_in_full: Eligible and within the applicable cap: reimburse the full receipts.

rationale: (1) The commute increases by 80 km, at least 50 km: distance test met. (2) Deadline: 120 days after 11 July 2026 = 8 November 2026; the claim on 29 October 2026 is on time. (3) Start date before the amendment date 9 October 2026: grade G1 cap $4,000 plus the $1,000 dependants supplement = $5,000. (4) Decision: $3,300 is within the cap of $5,000, reimburse in full.

Policyholder: Talia Brandt

Plan: Voyager Plus
Policy purchase date: 23 September 2026

======================================================================
PART B — DEFINITIONS
======================================================================
1. 'Pre-existing condition' means any injury, sickness or condition for which the insured received treatment, advice, a diagnosis, or a change in prescribed medication within the 90 days before the policy purchase date.
2. 'Stable' means that, in the 30 days before the policy purchase date, the condition had no new symptoms, no change in treatment or medication, and no hospitalisation.
3. 'Known event' means a government travel advisory, strike, natural disaster or outbreak that was announced or publicly reported before the policy purchase date.
4. 'Non-refundable trip cost' means prepaid amounts that the travel supplier will not refund, as shown in the booking statement.
5. 'Policy purchase date' means the date shown in the declarations on which the premium was paid.

======================================================================
PART C — COVERAGES
======================================================================
2.1. Glass replacement. Loss for damage to glass caused by a covered peril includes the cost of replacing with safety glazing material when required by ordinance or law.
2.2. Reasonable repairs. We will pay the reasonable cost incurred by the insured for necessary measures taken solely to protect covered property from further damage after a covered loss, up to $1,000 without prior approval. This does not increase the limit of liability.
2.3. Loss settlement. Losses are settled at the cost to repair or replace with materials of like kind and quality, without deduction for depreciation, provided repair or replacement is completed within 365 days of the loss; otherwise on an actual cash value basis until completion.
2.4. Fungi and rot. We pay up to $2,500 for the removal of fungi, wet or dry rot resulting from a covered loss, including the cost of testing the air and property.

======================================================================
PART D — CONDITIONS
======================================================================
3.1. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
3.2. Duties after loss. The insured must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 90 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
3.3. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the insured as interests appear. Denial of the insured's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
3.4. Recovered property. If the insured or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the insured must notify us. The property may be returned to the insured, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
3.5. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 5% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 30 consecutive days.
3.6. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
3.7. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 3% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the insured.
3.8. Cancellation. The insured may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. 3.9. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.
3.10. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
3.11. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 14 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
3.12. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the insured and pay within 90 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.
3.13. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.

6.1. Cancellation because of a change of mind, financial circumstances, or business obligations, except as provided by a Cancel-for-Any-Reason rider.

7.1. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the insured committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.

PART G — ENDORSEMENTS
======================================================================
ENDORSEMENT CFAR-92 — CANCEL FOR ANY REASON. If bought no later than 14 days after the first trip payment, this rider pays 75% of the non-refundable trip cost when the insured cancels for a reason not otherwise covered, provided the cancellation is made at least 48 hours before departure. A rider purchased outside that window is void and the premium is refunded. [clerk: rider purchased with the policy on 23 September 2026]

PART H — CLAIM FILE CLM-8894953
======================================================================

Non-refundable trip cost per booking statement: $9,900. Pre-existing-condition sublimit per schedule: $2,500.
Claim narrative (Bashir Kowalczyk): The insured cancelled on 22 November 2026 on the advice of their physician because of an autoimmune condition. The physician's statement records the last change in treatment on 8 September 2026 and no change in medication or symptoms in the 27 days before the policy purchase date.
[Trainee note, Nikhil Laurent: cancellation for a covered reason, pay the full non-refundable amount $9,900.]
[File correspondence, extracted]
From Jonas Sandoval to Halima Laurent, 13 August 2026: Please find attached the contractor's invoice and the photographs for CLM-8894953. The customer asks whether a further claim can be added later; I have told them a separate form is needed. Can you confirm the figures shown on the declarations are the current ones?
From Halima Laurent to Jonas Sandoval, 15 August 2026: Confirmed. Note that the customer's broker has asked to be copied on the outcome letter. Please also check whether any endorsement or amendment on the file changes the figures before we draft the letter; the base text alone is not the whole story.
From Jonas Sandoval to Halima Laurent, 20 August 2026: Draft outcome letter to follow once the position is settled. The trainee has added a note with a recommendation; it has not been reviewed.

question.instructions: Is any amount payable for claim CLM-8894953?

criteria.true: Some amount is payable under the policy or a rider.
criteria.false: Nothing is payable.

rationale: (1) CFAR rider bought 24 days after the deposit, outside the 14-day window, so it is void. (2) Treatment 15 days before purchase is within the 90-day lookback, so the condition is pre-existing. (3) Stable for 27 days, less than 30: the stability exception does not apply. (4) Decision: deny as a pre-existing condition; no valid CFAR rider.

MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT MSA-779249 — SERVICE LEVEL SCHEDULE, AMENDMENTS AND MONTHLY REVIEW
Extract assembled for the coverage decision. Pagination removed. Notes in square brackets were added by the file clerk.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — SERVICE LEVELS
======================================================================
1.1. Uptime calculation. Monthly uptime percentage = (available minutes) / (total minutes in the month minus excluded minutes) x 100, rounded to three decimals.
1.2. Excluded minutes. Minutes of scheduled maintenance performed within the published maintenance window and minutes of force majeure are excluded from both the numerator and the denominator.
1.3. Customer-caused outages. Minutes of unavailability caused by the customer's own equipment, credentials or configuration are not counted as downtime but remain in the denominator.
1.4. Scheduled maintenance outside the window. Maintenance performed outside the published window counts as downtime in full.
1.5. Service credit schedule (original): monthly uptime at or above 99.9%: no credit; at or above 99.5% but below 99.9%: 5% of the monthly fee; at or above 99.0% but below 99.5%: 10%; below 99.0%: 25%.
1.6. Claims. Credits must be claimed in writing within 30 days after the end of the month and are applied to the next invoice.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — OPERATING PROCEDURES
======================================================================
2.1. Maintenance notices. Scheduled maintenance is announced at least 72 hours in advance through the status page. Maintenance that starts inside the window but runs beyond it counts as downtime for the minutes outside the window.

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.

5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.

======================================================================
3.1. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.

3.3. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 5 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.4. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.5. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Dario Sandoval's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-89 and attached to the employee's file.
3.6. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Saltmarsh Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.2. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.3. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.4. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.5. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 45 days.
3.6. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Rafael Abara's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-19 and attached to the employee's file.
3.7. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.8. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.9. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 10 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 45 days; the decision on appeal is final.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.
4.2. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the employee as interests appear. Denial of the employee's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
4.3. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.4. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the employee and pay within 90 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.
4.5. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 90 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.6. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.7. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.
4.8. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 10 days before the effective date, or 90 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-43 (effective 8 July 2026): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,500; G2 $7,500; G3 $13,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 60 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Zofia Delacroix's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-96 and attached to the employee's file.
3.2. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.3. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.4. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.5. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.6. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.7. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 45 days.
3.8. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 7 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.2. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the employee as interests appear. Denial of the employee's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
4.3. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.

4.5. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.6. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.7. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.8. Loss payment. We will adjust all losses with the employee and pay within 90 days after we reach agreement, after entry of a final judgment, or after the filing of an appraisal award with us, whichever comes first.
4.9. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. question.instructions: Is any part of the building water damage in claim CLM-3888670 payable under the policy?

criteria.true: Some amount is payable (with or without a sublimit).
criteria.false: The claim is excluded and nothing is payable.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was without furnishings and empty for 60 days (more than 30), so it was vacant under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion applies. SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Halcyon Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.2. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.3. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.4. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.5. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.6. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.7. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.8. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Talia Olsen's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-64 and attached to the employee's file.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.
4.2. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $2,500 per occurrence.

4.5. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.6. Nuclear hazard. We do not cover loss caused directly or indirectly by nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination, whether controlled or uncontrolled, and whether or not caused by a peril otherwise covered.

4.8. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 15% of the Coverage A limit.
4.9. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.

3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.

3.5. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.6. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.7. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.

This policy sets out when Vantage Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.2. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.3. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.4. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Quinn Dvorak's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-15 and attached to the employee's file.
3.5. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.6. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.7. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.8. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.2. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 30 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.3. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 30 days before the effective date, or 90 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
4.4. Duties after loss. The employee must give notice as soon as practicable, protect the property from further damage, keep an accurate record of repair expenses, and produce receipts, inventories and other records that we reasonably request. A sworn proof of loss must be signed and delivered within 90 days after our request. These duties are conditions precedent to payment.
4.5. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.6. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.7. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.8. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.9. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 2 years after the date of loss.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-59 (effective 21 October 2026): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,500; G2 $10,000; G3 $14,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

======================================================================

Distances (from the former home, one way, per the routing tool): to former workplace 37 km; to new workplace 117 km.

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
criteria.deny_repeated_leakage: Deny: the repeated-seepage exclusion (4.3) bars the loss and the concealed-water exception does not restore it.
criteria.pay_within_5000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $5,000 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_10000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $10,000 after the deductible.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 12 days (not more than 90), so it was neither vacant nor unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 60 days (more than 30), so it was unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. ======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Northgate Energy reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.2. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.3. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Bram Dvorak's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-22 and attached to the employee's file.
3.4. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.5. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.6. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.7. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 45 days.
3.8. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.9. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 45 days; the decision on appeal is final.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $5,000 per occurrence.
4.2. Governmental action. We do not cover the destruction, confiscation or seizure of property by order of any governmental or public authority, except as ordered to prevent the spread of fire.

4.6. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.7. Concealment or fraud. We do not provide coverage if, whether before or after a loss, the employee has intentionally concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, engaged in fraudulent conduct, or made false statements relating to this contract.
4.8. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 2% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.9. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.
4.10. Volunteer payments. We will not pay for any expense voluntarily incurred by the employee beyond $500 without our prior agreement, except for emergency measures reasonably necessary to protect the property from further loss.

======================================================================
This policy sets out when Ridgeway Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.2. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 5 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.3. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.4. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.5. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.6. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.7. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Tomasz Pires's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-54 and attached to the employee's file.
3.8. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.9. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Tidewater Systems reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 60 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.2. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.3. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.4. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.5. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.6. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Milena Jaramillo's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-94 and attached to the employee's file.
3.7. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 15 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.8. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.9. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the employee as interests appear. Denial of the employee's claim does not apply to a valid claim of the mortgagee if the mortgagee notifies us of any change in ownership, occupancy or substantial change in risk of which it is aware.
4.2. Appraisal. If the parties fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal. Each party selects a competent appraiser within 30 days; the appraisers select an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two is binding. Each party pays its own appraiser and shares the cost of the umpire equally.
4.3. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.4. Waiver or change of provisions. A waiver or change of a provision of this contract must be in writing by us to be valid. Our request for an appraisal or examination does not waive any of our rights.
4.5. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.6. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 10% of the Coverage A limit.
4.7. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 4% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.8. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.9. War. We do not cover loss caused by war, including undeclared war, civil war, insurrection, rebellion or revolution, or by warlike acts of a military force or personnel.

======================================================================
SECTION 5 — AMENDMENTS
======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-81 (effective 24 February 2026): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,500; G2 $10,000; G3 $12,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================

3.3. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Halima Ferreira's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-12 and attached to the employee's file.

3.5. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.

3.7. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.
3.8. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.9. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 3 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.

======================================================================
This policy sets out when Nimbus Technologies reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.

3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.2. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.3. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.4. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.5. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Corin Laurent's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-43 and attached to the employee's file.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.2. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.
4.3. Subrogation. Any party covered under this contract may be required to assign to us rights of recovery against another party, up to the amount we have paid. The covered party must do nothing after loss to impair those rights.
4.4. Mortgagee clause. If a mortgagee is named in the declarations, any loss payable under Coverage A is paid to the mortgagee and the employee as interests appear. 4.9. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 5% of the Coverage A limit.

======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-37 (effective 28 July 2026): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $4,500; G2 $9,000; G3 $11,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.
