======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Stonebridge Energy reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 60 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 5 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.2. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.3. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.4. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.5. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.6. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Bram Jaramillo's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-98 and attached to the employee's file.
3.7. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.8. Audit. Internal audit samples 10% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Salvage. When we pay for a loss we may take all or part of the damaged property at an agreed or appraised value. There is no abandonment of property to us.
4.2. Other insurance. If a loss covered by this contract is also covered by other insurance, we will pay only the proportion of the loss that the limit of liability that applies under this contract bears to the total amount of insurance covering the loss.
4.3. Suit against us. No action can be brought against us unless there has been full compliance with all of the terms of this contract and the action is started within 2 years after the date of loss.
4.4. Neglect. We do not cover loss that results from the employee failing to take reasonable steps to protect and preserve the property once a loss has occurred.
4.5. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.
4.6. Electronic data. Loss of or damage to electronic data is covered only for the cost of blank media and the cost of copying from backups, subject to a limit of $5,000 per occurrence.
4.7. Ordinance or law. Extra cost caused by having to comply with building codes or other regulations when repairing, rebuilding or demolishing is covered up to 15% of the Coverage A limit.
4.8. Cancellation. The employee may cancel at any time by returning the contract to us or by notifying us in writing of the date cancellation is to take effect. We may cancel by mailing notice at least 21 days before the effective date, or 90 days where the cancellation is for reasons other than non-payment. Unearned premium is refunded pro rata.
4.9. Inflation guard. The limits shown in the declarations increase by 3% at each anniversary of the inception date unless this endorsement is deleted by the employee.
4.10. Recovered property. If the employee or we recover any property for which we have made payment, the employee must notify us. The property may be returned to the employee, in which case the loss payment is adjusted accordingly.
4.11. Territorial limits. Coverage applies to losses occurring within the territory shown in the declarations. Property temporarily removed from the premises is covered for up to 15% of the applicable limit, but not for more than 30 consecutive days.
4.12. Assignment. Assignment of this contract is not valid unless we give our written consent.

======================================================================
AMENDMENT A-52 (effective 13 February 2026): for relocations where the employee's start date at the new workplace is on or after the effective date, the caps in rule 3 are increased to G1 $5,500; G2 $10,000; G3 $12,500. Relocations with earlier start dates remain on the previous caps.

criteria.deny_vacant_dwelling: Deny: the vacancy exclusion (4.7) bars the building water damage and no exception restores cover.
criteria.deny_repeated_leakage: Deny: the repeated-seepage exclusion (4.3) bars the loss and the concealed-water exception does not restore it.
criteria.pay_within_7500_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $7,500 after the deductible.
criteria.pay_within_10000_sublimit: Pay: cover is restored by the concealed-water exception, capped at $10,000 after the deductible.

rationale: (1) The dwelling was furnished and empty for 59 days (not more than 60), so it was neither vacant nor unoccupied under the definitions. (2) The vacancy exclusion does not apply. SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Cinder Industries reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 60 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $10,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================

======================================================================

======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 50 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 90 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $4,000; G2 $7,500; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $1,500.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.2. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.3. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.4. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.5. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 20 days.
3.6. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 20 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.7. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.8. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Leif Ishida's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-34 and attached to the employee's file.

======================================================================
SECTION 4 — GENERAL PROVISIONS
======================================================================
4.1. Intentional loss. We do not cover loss caused by an act that the employee committed, or directed someone else to commit, intending the loss to happen.

Extract assembled for the coverage decision. Pagination removed. Notes in square brackets were added by the file clerk.

======================================================================
SECTION 1 — PURPOSE AND SCOPE
======================================================================
This policy sets out when Northgate Industries reimburses relocation costs for employees who move at the company's request. It applies to all grades and locations.

======================================================================
SECTION 2 — RULES
======================================================================
1. Eligibility (distance test). A relocation is eligible only if the one-way distance from the employee's former home to the new workplace exceeds the distance from the former home to the former workplace by at least 80 km.
2. Time limit. Claims must be submitted with receipts within 120 days of the employee's start date at the new workplace. Where the employee is on approved leave during that period, the limit is extended by the number of leave days.
3. Caps. Reimbursement is capped by grade: G1 $3,000; G2 $6,000; G3 $12,000. Amounts above the cap are not reimbursed.
4. Dependants supplement. Where a spouse, partner or dependent child moves with the employee, the cap is increased by $2,000.
5. Excluded costs. Costs of buying or selling a home, mortgage penalties, and temporary accommodation beyond 30 nights are not reimbursable under this policy.
6. Repayment. An employee who leaves the company within 12 months of the start date must repay the reimbursement pro rata.

======================================================================
SECTION 3 — PROCESS
======================================================================
3.1. Approvals. A relocation must be approved in writing by the receiving manager and by HR (Aiko Fontaine's team) before the move date. Approval is recorded on form RL-56 and attached to the employee's file.
3.2. Receipts. Only itemised receipts in the employee's name are accepted. Credit-card statements alone are not sufficient. Receipts in a foreign currency are converted at the company's monthly rate for the month of the expense.
3.3. Appeals. An employee may appeal a decision under this policy within 5 business days by writing to the HR director. The appeal is decided within 30 days; the decision on appeal is final.
3.4. Definitions. 'Start date' means the first day the employee is required to attend the new workplace, as stated in the transfer letter. 'Former home' means the address on file on the date of the transfer letter.
3.5. Tax treatment. Reimbursements are reported in accordance with local tax rules. Where a reimbursement is taxable, the amount paid to the employee is not grossed up unless the offer letter says otherwise.
3.6. Interaction with other policies. Travel on the move day is reimbursed under this policy, not under the travel policy. Costs reimbursed under this policy are not claimable again under any other policy.
3.7. Data protection. Documents submitted with a claim are kept for 5 years after the claim is closed and are accessible only to HR and to the auditors.
3.8. Audit. Internal audit samples 5% of relocation claims each year. A claim found to be inaccurate may be recovered from salary in accordance with the deductions policy.
3.9. Temporary accommodation. Where temporary accommodation is reimbursed, the employee must move to permanent accommodation within 30 nights; extensions require the approval of the HR director.
3.10. Advances. An advance of up to 50% of the applicable cap may be requested before the move; it is deducted from the final reimbursement. Unused advances must be repaid within 30 days.

======================================================================
